title: CrossModal Study
description: The CrossModal Study is an EEG dataset investigating how the brain prepares for and discriminates targets across sensory modalities. Participants received cues to prepare for auditory, visual, or non-specific targets, followed by a 3-second interval with frequency-tagged visual stimulation (36 Hz) and amplitude-modulated auditory stimulation (40 Hz). Targets were either Gabor patches or tones, with cross-modal distractors presented in cued conditions. The dataset comprises 28 experimental blocks per participant and includes EOG recordings to monitor eye activity.
methods_description: EEG data were collected from healthy control participants with normal or corrected-to-normal vision and no history of psychiatric or neurological illness. The experimental protocol involved six randomly ordered and balanced conditions combining cue type (auditory, visual, non-specific) with target modality and distractor presence. Participants performed target discrimination tasks using keyboard responses. One additional EOG channel was acquired to monitor eye activity. Data were collected at Birmingham University, United Kingdom.
